author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A single-page piece from the Berkeley Daily Gazette (February 7, 1944), written when Dick was about fifteen—childhood apprentice work preserved as a marker of his earliest writing rather than mature fiction.
page_summary:
The Magician's Box is a very short item Dick placed in the Berkeley Daily Gazette on February 7, 1944, when he was around fifteen. It survives as a one-page scan and belongs to the body of juvenilia he produced as a teenager contributing to the local paper.

Its significance is documentary. It shows Dick continuing to write and publish through his adolescence, in the years between his first childhood newspaper pieces and the professional science-fiction sales that began in 1952. The archive preserves it as a dated trace of that formative stretch.

Given its length, the piece is best understood as an early exercise rather than a developed story. It is one small entry in the record of how persistently Dick wrote from a young age, long before his characteristic themes emerged.
